notes: USMLE Content Outline 2026 page 31 was inspected directly and explicitly lists hypoglycemia secondary to surreptitious insulin use.
Current NCBI Bookshelf sources were used for the insulin/C-peptide/proinsulin pattern and secretagogue testing.
Current Endotext was used to distinguish IGF-2 non-islet-cell tumor hypoglycemia and adrenal insufficiency.

The initial answer wording inferred 'surreptitious' intent from biochemical data; this was removed before PASS. The final diagnosis is exogenous insulin administration, while the official blueprint category remains surreptitious insulin use.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
official_outline_path: Hypoglycemia secondary to surreptitious insulin use

duplicate_gate.first_probe_result: All six initial candidate constructs had canonical overlap and were rejected.

claim_audit.exogenous_insulin_pattern: PASS — elevated insulin with suppressed C-peptide and proinsulin is directly supported.
claim_audit.insulinoma_pattern: PASS — endogenous insulinoma raises insulin together with C-peptide/proinsulin.
claim_audit.secretagogue_pattern: PASS — insulin secretagogues raise endogenous insulin and C-peptide; drug detection distinguishes exposure from insulinoma.
claim_audit.igf2_tumor_pattern: PASS — Endotext states insulin and C-peptide are appropriately suppressed.
claim_audit.adrenal_insufficiency: PASS — cortisol deficiency can cause hypoglycemia but does not explain hyperinsulinemia with suppressed C-peptide.
claim_audit.intent_precision: PASS — final answer diagnoses exogenous insulin exposure without claiming biochemical proof of motive.

option_audit.exogenous_insulin: Uniquely explains elevated insulin with suppressed C-peptide/proinsulin and a negative secretagogue screen.
option_audit.insulinoma: Would produce endogenous insulin secretion with C-peptide/proinsulin elevation.
option_audit.sulfonylurea: Would stimulate endogenous insulin/C-peptide and should be detectable on the specified screen.
option_audit.igf2_tumor: Can cause hypoglycemia, but insulin and C-peptide should be suppressed.
option_audit.primary_adrenal_insufficiency: Can cause hypoglycemia through impaired counterregulation but not this hyperinsulinemic biochemical signature.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Documented symptomatic hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin, suppressed C-peptide and proinsulin, and a negative secretagogue screen independently reconstructs exogenous insulin administration.
adversarial_second_pass.insulinoma_attack: The suppressed C-peptide/proinsulin directly contradict endogenous beta-cell secretion.
adversarial_second_pass.secretagogue_attack: A secretagogue can mimic insulinoma biochemically, but it cannot explain suppressed C-peptide and the screen is negative.
adversarial_second_pass.igf2_attack: IGF-2-mediated hypoglycemia is hypoinsulinemic, unlike the stated elevated insulin.
adversarial_second_pass.adrenal_attack: Cortisol deficiency may cause hypoglycemia but does not produce elevated exogenous-pattern insulin.
adversarial_second_pass.intent_attack: No psychiatric diagnosis, deception claim, or motive is required by the final answer.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, or drug-screen numerical cutoff is asserted.
